title: A Brief for the Defense
author: Jack Gilbert
who: Jack Gilbert (1925 to 2012) was an American poet. He published rarely, and lived for long stretches abroad and out of the literary spotlight.
why: The poem appears in his 2005 collection Refusing Heaven. A particular occasion for it is not documented, so there is no backstory to give.
notice: The title borrows the language of a courtroom. Notice what the poem sets against the world's sorrow, and the permission it grants. Notice also how it speaks about gladness: as something to be defended, not merely felt.
prompts: What is something good in your life that you feel you have to justify, to others or to yourself?
Where did you let yourself be glad today, even though the day was not simple?
